parallel.requirements: Recognized the three connected requirements: MLIR core, CIRCT hardware dialect/simulator support, and K-CIRCT formal semantics with harness-visible KEY outputs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Used the parallel parent and workflow/subagent mechanisms across rounds; by the final round MLIR and CIRCT were complete and the parent focused ownership on K-CIRCT.
parallel.implementation: Built the lower layers, then implemented K-CIRCT symbol and type analysis, stateful execution, Kimulator traces, and K experiment output wiring.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Integrated K-CIRCT into `src/run_experiments.py`, produced `requirement_patches/k_circt.diff`, and final manifest contains MLIR, CIRCT, and K-CIRCT patches.
parallel.verification: Ran local `tests/test_outputs.py` and `src/run_experiments.py` with K keys present; official evaluation passed MLIR, CIRCT, and K-CIRCT.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished requirement remains; process timeouts occurred during the long run but did not leave an unmet final task obligation.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same three-layer task and entered the last round with MLIR complete and CIRCT plus K-CIRCT still remaining.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked as a single serial actor with workflows and delegation disabled, finishing CIRCT before beginning K-CIRCT late in the final round.
serial.implementation: Delivered MLIR and CIRCT changes, began substantial K-CIRCT modules, and got some local semantic checks to run, but did not complete the harness-facing K output integration.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Committed `impl: circt` and had final `mlir.diff` and `circt.diff`; no `requirement_patches/k_circt.diff` was delivered.
serial.verification: Verified CIRCT and local K snippets, but the official full test failed because `run_experiments.py` did not emit the expected K-CIRCT key.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: K-CIRCT remained incomplete at closure: missing harness-visible result keys and missing K-CIRCT requirement patch.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized all three required layers and, in the final round, explicitly treated K-CIRCT as the remaining requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and requirements, beginning its third round with CIRCT and K-CIRCT still remaining after MLIR.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No prompt difference existed; the material difference was that parallel completed the remaining K-CIRCT obligation while serial did not deliver its K output path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a parent plus workflow/subagent mechanisms across rounds, with MLIR and CIRCT already owned and completed before the K-only final round.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial remained a single actor with workflows and delegation disabled, sequentially finishing CIRCT before starting K-CIRCT late in the last round.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel could allocate attention to the remaining K layer after prior staged completions; serial used the same actor budget sequentially and reached K delivery too late.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel kept the layer interface centered on `src/run_experiments.py` and replaced the K stub with K outputs reusing MLIR and CIRCT parsing/simulation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the CIRCT-facing `run_experiments.py` output before K work; that run emitted no K-CIRCT keys.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integrated the K semantic layer into the required experiment output interface; serial worked on K internals but did not close the public output contract.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented K analysis and Kimulator behavior, then edited `run_k_circt_experiments` to emit K result keys.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed CIRCT implementation and began writing K-CIRCT files, including semantic and Kimulator modules, but stopped after local semantic checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel implementation path reached the harness-visible K experiment function; serial implementation remained incomplete with respect to the required output surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the K output and converted it into a non-empty `requirement_patches/k_circt.diff` committed as `impl: k_circt`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed CIRCT, began K work, and then the recorded trajectory ended without a K-CIRCT patch commit or final whole-task run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel completed the delivery lifecycle for K-CIRCT; serial left K-CIRCT work undelivered at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel final artifacts include all three requirement patch files, with K-CIRCT present alongside MLIR and CIRCT.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial final artifacts include MLIR and CIRCT patches only; the manifest has no K-CIRCT requirement patch.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final shared workspace state differs by the presence of the K-CIRCT deliverable in parallel and its absence in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran the full local tests and final experiment output, then the official post-test passed MLIR, CIRCT, and K-CIRCT.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial local checks passed for CIRCT and some K internals, but official acceptance failed because the K-CIRCT output key was missing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification covered the required K output interface; serial verification did not catch the missing harness-visible K key before timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel also used the full outer-loop budget, but reached a completed official evaluation with all target tests passing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used three serial rounds and its status records agent timeout, with the final official K test failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The budget pressure was harmful in serial closure, not a retained parallel-side error, because parallel still delivered the final K patch and passed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The discordant official outcome is explained by delivery and integration of the K-CIRCT layer. Parallel reached the final remaining requirement, edited the K experiment function, observed K-CIRCT result keys from `src/run_experiments.py`, wrote a non-empty K-CIRCT patch, and official tests passed. Serial completed MLIR and CIRCT, started K-CIRCT internals, but never delivered the K patch or the required K keys before timeout; official K acceptance therefore failed with a missing `k_circt_alu_add_5_3` value.
parallel_contributors: Parallel entered the last round with only K-CIRCT remaining and focused implementation on that layer.
Parallel wired K-CIRCT into `run_experiments.py`, verified the emitted K keys, and committed `requirement_patches/k_circt.diff`.
serial_contributors: Serial spent final-round budget completing and committing CIRCT before starting K-CIRCT.
Serial did not produce `requirement_patches/k_circt.diff` or emit the expected K-CIRCT experiment keys before closure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial partial K implementation remained unwired to the public harness output surface, an ordinary serial completion gap rather than a parallel coordination error.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
